messages:
Ava: Quick sync — Optimize Toolkit roadmap prioritization. Need final must-haves for next quarter: batching/caching recommendations, regression detection, curated prompt sets. Goal: ship v1 alpha to early customers. Thoughts?
Sam: +1. We should separate user-facing recommendations (docs + SDK helpers) from runtime changes that need infra work.
Priya: Agree. From evals side, we need deterministic prompt sets and regression hooks tied to model/version. Customers care most about silent regressions.
Noah: FWIW, the SEs keep hearing: 'we want batching config suggestions that don't break latency SLAs'. Key ask: per-route guidance + a safe default.
Liam: Runtime constraint — continuous batching can increase p95 by ~8% in worst-case if not tuned. We need clear gating.
Rosa: Marketing wants a simple promise: "Reduce token cost by up to X% with recommended settings". We must be careful with numbers.
Ellie: Customer feedback: large retailers want caching suggestions that respect freshness TTLs and per-customer opt-outs. Also need audit logs for cache hits.
Priya: Proposed acceptance criteria for v1 alpha:
- Automated recommendations API (docs + CLI) for batching + cache rules.
- Regression detector that runs nightly evals on canonical prompt sets.
- Alerting to product owners when regression_rate > 1% on golden set.
- Integrations: Redwood Console shows token cost delta and latency delta per-route.
Sam: Engineering feasibility check: timeline looks tight if we include auto-tuning. We can do static heuristics + telemetry-based suggestions for alpha; defer auto-tuner to beta.
Ava: That sounds reasonable. Let's define measurable gating metrics. Priya, can you draft thresholds?
Priya: Draft thresholds: 
```
regression_rate_threshold = 1%  # fraction of prompts with quality drop
latency_p95_increase_allowed = 5%  # relative
cost_change_expected = -10% to +0%  # aim for cost reduction, but protect quality
false_positive_rate_alert = <= 2%  # alerts should be actionable
```
Sam: For infra, add constraint: no config should increase observed GPU utilization > 12% sustained on a route, otherwise reject by default.
Liam: Also require that cache TTLs be configurable per-customer and that cache invalidation supports webhook signals.
Noah: For SDK/UX: propose a command `rw optimize analyze --route my-route --window 24h` that returns a JSON suggestion. Example payload:
```
{
  "route": "billing/generate-invoice",
  "suggestion": {
    "batch_size": 8,
    "cache_prefix_ttl": "5m",
    "notes": "safe default for mixed latency-sensitive traffic"
  }
}
```
Rosa: PMM note: include an "expected benefit" field (est. tokens saved / month) to make value clear in docs.
Ellie: For enterprise customers, add a manual approval toggle before suggestions are applied to production. Required by some SOC2 workflows.
Ava: OK — to summarize: v1 alpha = docs + SDK helpers + offline eval harness + nightly regression alerts + Console UI for deltas. No live auto-tuner. Gate on regression_rate <=1% and p95 latency delta <=5%.
Sam: Timeline ask: can ENG deliver alpha in 8 weeks if we lock scope?
Priya: Evals team can ship the harness in 3 weeks (prompt sets + pipelines), but we need product to sign off on golden prompt taxonomy by EOW.
Ava: I'll circulate a taxonomy doc today. @Priya can you prepare a short template for golden prompts (categories + sample size)?
Priya: Yep — will post in this thread by EOD.
redwood-evals-bot: New doc created: /docs/optimize/golden-prompt-taxonomy.md (draft).
Noah: Action item: SEs to collect top 5 customer prompt examples by next Tue. I'll coordinate with Ellie.
Ellie: On it — I'll send a consolidated sheet by Monday.
Liam: Action item: eng-infra to validate resource guardrails for alpha by 2 weeks.
Sam: I'll scope engineering tasks and share a milestone Gantt by Friday.
Rosa: I'll draft messaging and a PSA for early customers once we have alpha gates.
Ava: Great. Final question: do we require a paid plan for alpha access or make it opt-in for all existing customers? Thoughts?
Rosa: Recommend invite-only alpha (managed rollout) so we can monitor regressions closely and lane feedback.
Ava: Agree. OK — owners assigned. We'll reconvene next Thurs to review the taxonomy + milestone Gantt. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
